Program/Service Description: The 5th Dimension Outdoor Club was established as an organization for the purpose of providing active older adults, 55 years of age and older, with the opportunity to participate in outdoor activities as a group. The club offers activities such as hiking, cross-country skiing, snowshoe, and year round day trips every Thursdays. During the summer months they also offer the opportunity to golf in Calgary with other older adults in The Club on Wednesdays. The group also hosts seasonal gatherings, such as a summer potluck and a Christmas lunch.
Short Description: Activities include hiking, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and year-round day trips every Thursday. Golf is offered in the summer.
Cost Details: Annual membership fees are $50/year, reduced to $25/year for new members joining in the spring. $25 per bus trip, payable on the bus. Email organizers for more details

Short Description: Provides transportation for individuals with complex medical and mobility challenges within Calgary and surrounding communities.

Program/Service Description: Kanakaa’tsinom, meaning “All Friends Place” in Blackfoot, is Calgary’s first-ever Indigenous Elders Drop-in Centre. It provides a compassionate and welcoming space for Calgary’s vulnerable older adults. Programming includes traditional ceremonies, language revitalization, support services, cultural crafts (like ribbon shirt making), Bingo, shared meals, and opportunities to connect.
Short Description: Programming includes traditional ceremonies, language revitalization, support services, cultural crafts (like ribbon shirt making), Bingo, shared meals, and opportunities to connect.
How to Access: Elders can drop in anytime the Centre is open or contact Eugene Wilk to inquire about specific events.
Email: Eugene Wilk (Program Manager, ewilk@afccalgary.org, or Vada Hoof (Program Support Staff, vhoof@afccalgary.org).

Program/Service Description: Beyond the core programs at the Drop-in Centre and the Lodge, AFCC provides and facilitates Elder support in numerous ways. AFCC has coordinated essential health services, such as a Vaccination Clinic that administered over 400 vaccinations to Elders in a culturally sensitive environment. AFCC facilitates intergenerational connections, creating opportunities like the Elders & Youth Gathering at the Lodge and sharing circles where Elders impart wisdom directly to youth.
Short Description: AFCC offers a Vaccination Clinic that administers vaccines in a culturally safe environment. They also facilitate intergenerational connections between Elders and youth.
Email: Eugene Wilk (Program Manager, ewilk@afccalgary.org, or Vada Hoof (Program Support Staff, vhoof@afccalgary.org). General inquiries: info@afccalgary.org
Address: 4630 16 Ave NW, Calgary. See contact page for full list of locations.

Program/Service Description: AFCC assists community members in obtaining or renewing their Secure Certificate of Indian Status (Status Card) and now offers registration services under the Indian Act. This means AFCC can also help eligible individuals apply to be registered for the first time.
Short Description: Receive support in obtaining or renewing your Secure Certificate of Indian Status (Status Card).
How to Access: If you are already registered and renewing your status card, please bring: Your 10-digit registration (treaty) number, one valid piece of government-issued photo ID. If you are applying for registration for the first time, you will need: One valid piece of government-issued photo ID, a long-form birth certificate that includes parentage, knowledge of your family tree (e.g., parent and grandparent names, communities). Additional documentation may be required depending on the complexity of your case.

Program/Service Description: AFCC provides navigation and support services for vulnerable and unhoused community members, operating out of the Salvation Army Centre of Hope. The goal of this program is to act as a centralized hub connecting individuals to a network of services addressing root causes of homelessness and addiction (mental health, housing, recovery programs, employment, social services). A key goal is integrating Indigenous ways of knowing, traditional healing practices (access to Elders, ceremonies like smudging, talking circles), and spirituality into service delivery for holistic healing.
Short Description: Navigation and support services for vulnerable and unhoused community members that is integrated with Indigenous ways of knowing and traditional healing practices.
Eligibility Criteria: Vulnerable and unhoused individuals in Calgary, with a focus on culturally safe support for Indigenous peoples.
Address: Salvation Army Centre of Hope, 420 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB T2G 0R9.

It will ask you questions in four categories: finances, care and assistance, lifestyle, and location. Based on your answers to the questions, the tool will suggest places where you can find more information and help.
Short Description: Provides information about housing options that are tailored to your needs.
How to Access: Online, or contact organizers for help using this tool

Program/Service Description: The goal of the Pet Food Assistance Program is to prevent pets from ending up in shelters or rescues by offering assistance to individuals or families experiencing financial challenges or hardships.
Short Description: Offers assistance to individuals or families experiencing financial challenges to prevent pets from ending up in shelters.
Eligibility Criteria: Complete a request form online. Eligible individuals must live in Calgary

Program/Service Description: If you are unable to keep your pet, AARC will aim to find them a new home. Space is limited in shelters, and placement for your pet may take several days or even weeks. All public intake requests require pre-approval and are not guaranteed.
Short Description: If you are unable to keep your pet, AARC will aim to find them a new home.
Eligibility Criteria: Complete a request form online. Eligible individuals must live in Calgary.  Intake approval will vary depending on the needs of the animal, the space they have available in care, as well as resources available to them to address any medical or behavioural needs.
Cost Details: Should AARCS be in a position to accept your pet, a Care Contribution Fee between $50 to $100 may be required.

Program/Service Description: This initiative is designed to be a compassionate, low-barrier option to help older adults access essential care for their furry companions. These one-day clinics will provide basic wellness exams and vaccinations to help ensure the health and well-being of pets in our community.
Short Description: One-day clinics will provide basic wellness exams and vaccinations for pets.
Eligibility Criteria: Be 65 years of age or older, have reliable transportation to bring your pet to and from the Wellness Clinic, and complete the form online and receive pre-approval
How to Access: Complete a request form online. Applications are currently closed

Short Description: Basic and advanced foot care to clients in clinic settings, facilities and at home.

Whether you’re starting at the very beginning, or you just want to improve your online skills, our self-guided courses will meet you where you’re at and help you learn new skills quickly. Digital literacy courses are organized into two streams: the Beginner Program, for those who are pretty new to computers and using the internet, and the Intermediate Program, for those with some pre-existing knowledge.
Short Description: Learn how to use the internet through self-guided courses. There is a Beginner and an Intermediate stream.

Program areas include: active lifestyle, cooking food and nutrition, employment, finance and computer, health management, cancer and chronic conditions, Indigenous wellness, and more. Program/Service Description: This service provides comprehensive interprofessional palliative care services to adult patients and families who are living with a progressive life limiting illness or are nearing end of life. Service providers may include: doctors, licensed practical nurses (LPNs), nurse practitioners (NPs), occupational therapists (OTs), palliative care consultants, physiotherapists, registered nurses (RNs), respiratory therapists (RTs), social workers, spiritual care. Services are provided in home
Short Description: Provides comprehensive interprofessional palliative care services to adult patients and families who are living with a progressive life limiting illness or are nearing end of life.
Eligibility Criteria: Has a progressive advanced life threatening or end stage disease or illness with anticipated prognosis of less than 12 months; disease based interventions are primarily intended for symptom management and / improve quality of life; patient or family aware of diagnosis and prognosis and in agreement with a palliative approach to care; requires ongoing expertise of a specialized palliative care interprofessional team; an advance care planning or serious illness conversation has been initiated with the patient / family; the client is 18 years or older; the client is a resident of Alberta or is the process of setting up residency in Alberta
How to Access: Contact organizers. Patients and families can self-refer. Referrals are triaged daily based on urgency. You can expect to be seen within 24 hours to 7 days
Cost Details: There are no fees for professional or personal care services. There may be fees for equipment, supplies or medications.
Service Area: ["Advance care & future planning", "Physical health", "Grief & loss", "Home care"]

Program/Service Description: The Mental Help Line is a 24 hour, 7 day a week confidential service that provides support, information and referrals to Albertans experiencing mental health concerns. The line is staffed by a multidisciplinary team comprised of nurses, psychiatric nurses, social workers, occupational therapists, and psychologists. The service provides: confidential, anonymous service; information about mental health programs and services
Short Description: The Mental Help Line is a 24/7 confidential service that provides support, information and referrals to Albertans experiencing mental health concerns.

Program/Service Description: The support line is for First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples including youth and Elders, living on or off reserve, in a Settlement or in cities and towns. Indigenous listeners will answer your questions and help you get culturally appropriate care. They also help guide you on each step of your healthcare journey. Indigenous listeners are healthcare advisors. They answer and assist all callers to the support line. They can also arrange translators for callers.
Short Description: This support line is for Indigenous people who are looking to access culturally appropriate healthcare.
Eligibility Criteria: First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples living on or off reserve

Short Description: Provides community-based treatment for people with a moderate to severe mental illness.

Program/Service Description: Access MH is a non-urgent service providing telephone based screening / needs assessment, consultation, service navigation and referral. Clinicians are familiar with Alberta Health Services, Recovery Alberta Services and community-based programs and will explore all available options to make the most recommendations for the identified clinical need. It provides a single point of access for individuals of all ages residing in the Calgary Zone who are experiencing addiction and/or mental health concerns.
Short Description: A non-urgent mental health service providing telephone based screening / needs assessment, consultation, service navigation and referral.

Program/Service Description: Single session therapy available for clients of all ages 7 days per week by appointment only. Sessions are offered in-person at South Calgary Health Centre (SCHC). A single session of therapy can support individuals needing support with a particular concern or issue. Therapists may consult with one another to provide a collaborative approach. This service utilizes a teaching and consultative model and may have other therapists observing the session. This service does not offer mental health assessment or medication review. There is no access to psychiatry.
Short Description: Single session therapy available for clients of all ages 7 days per week by appointment only.
Address: South Calgary Health Centre: 31 Sunpark Plaza SE. North entrance, main floor. Check in at Outpatient Admitting desk

Program/Service Description: Since 1973, the Commission has overseen Alberta’s human rights legislation, affirming the fundamental principle that all persons are equal in the province. If you have been the victim of a human rights violation at work, with housing, while accessing public goods or services, or other scenarios, you can make a complaint to the commission. Start by completing a self-assessment to see if your complaint would be likely to fall in the Alberta Human Rights Act.
Short Description: Portal to make a complaint with the Human Rights Commission for rights violations related to work, housing, accessing public goods or services, or other scenarios.
Eligibility Criteria: N/A. The Commission can only accept complaints that include specific elements required by the Alberta Human Rights Act.
How to Access: Complete self-assessment online: https://albertahumanrights.ab.ca/complaints/am-i-in-the-right-place/self-assessment/. You can also call the confidential inquiry line.
Cost Details: The self-assessment is free to complete. The Commission does not require the complainant or respondent to be represented by a lawyer throughout the process. However, you may need or want someone to represent you during the process. The website includes a resource page with free and at-cost legal support.

Program/Service Description: The Calgary 55 Plus Hockey Association was formed in 1990 to provide an opportunity for Calgary and area players 55 years and older to participate in recreational hockey for the fun of the game.  Association members play in various arenas around the city, join in the camaraderie and fellowship, and support community programs through annual contributions to selected charities. There are currently twelve teams playing out of the South Fish Creek Cardel Rec Centre with one team playing out of each of the Optimist Arena, Renfrew Arena and Norma Bush City of Calgary Arenas.  The teams primarily play in the mornings and early afternoon. Our season runs from October 1 to March 31.  All of our teams play in the mornings from Monday to Friday.  Our players range in age from 55 to 89. Prospective players are tried to be placed on teams with similar skill and ability.

Groups are led by volunteers who have received Supported Conversation for Adults with Aphasia (SCA) training. They focus on enhancing people's existing skills and developing strategies that will reduce the barriers to their life participation goals. Groups are held at wheelchair accessible locations around Calgary and virtually on Zoom.
Short Description: Weekly conversation groups that offer people with aphasia and related communication disabilities to develop their communication skills and build social connections.
Eligibility Criteria: Individuals living with aphasia and related communication disabilities due to stroke or brain injury. Self referrals accepted. How to Access: To attend a CAC program you must first: 1) Complete the online registration form (link: https://calgaryaphasia.com/register/registration-patients/), 2) Speak with an intake coordinator, and 3) Be contacted by staff when a group is available.

Program/Service Description: The Digital Literacy for Newcomers (DLN) program offers newcomers the chance to build essential digital skills and confidence in today’s technology-driven world. Learners may choose to attend all four levels or select the ones that best meet their needs. Classes are primarily conducted in-person to facilitate student interactions and maximize engagement. Program/Service Description: The Calgary Humane Society is proud to offer resources to support vulnerable and isolated seniors with pets to ensure they can maintain this powerful connection with their companion animals. Resources include: Medical support; Euthanasia and cremation services support; Food bank services including prescription diets; Community engagement and volunteer opportunities; Affordable adoption fees. The Seniors Program assists seniors with companion animals by connecting them to veterinary services and assisting with the payment of care. The scope of the program will include single-treatment veterinary care to ensure the health and safety of their pet. However, treatment associated with lifelong diagnoses, ongoing care, or long-term medication will not be covered within the program.

Program/Service Description: The Everyday English for Seniors program focuses on enhancing the English language skills of immigrant seniors, both in oral and written communication. Participants receive valuable information about community resources available to support their integration process in Canada. The program offers field trips that provide practical opportunities for seniors to apply their English language skills in real-life situations. Sessions are held Monday to Friday, with morning (9:30 am – 12 pm) and afternoon (1 pm – 3:30 pm) time slots available.

Eligibility Criteria: The Everyday English for Seniors program is open to male and female immigrants who are 55 years old and above. It is available to Canadian citizens, permanent residents, refugees, and refugee claimants who may face financial barriers.

Program/Service Description: The Calgary Chapter lists more than 3,500 members. Plus, there are more than 14,000 throughout Alberta. CARP is a non-profit, non-partisan membership organization dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for all Canadians as we age. They advocate on policy issues related to Health Care, Financial Security, and against age discrimination, ensuring that all citizens have the right to continue working, driving and living independently for as long as possible, with financial and physical security. CARP provides a variety of savings through our affinity partners. Check with the National Website for more information. The membership tries to have meetings four times a year, including one annual general meeting in May where we select our organizing committees. Other special events are held during the year, sometimes in the form of information presentations, and sometimes just for fun. Members are kept in touch with local activities, events and promotions through the CARP website and through our CARP Calgary Facebook page and a chapter newsletter emailed to all members who have supplied an e-mail address.
Short Description: Advocy on policy issues related to Health Care, Financial Security, and against age discrimination. Members are kept in touch with local activities, events and promotions.
Cost Details: 1 year membership: $19.95. 2 year membership: $29.95. Additional $5 for a plastic membership card mailed to you

Program/Service Description: The Elder Abuse Response Team is a joint response with Calgary Police Service constables and Carya’s Specialized Criminal Justice Navigators (SCJNs), who respond together to victims of suspected and confirmed criminal cases of elder abuse. The police constables and SCJNs work in collaboration, with police conducting the investigative and risk assessment activities and the SCJNs focusing on the development of safety plans, resource requirements, comprehensive victim assessment, and ongoing emotional and resource supports for the victim. Working collaboratively with community partners, this program provides social work and outreach support to victims of non-criminal elder abuse.

Program/Service Description: The Centre for Equitable Library Access, CELA, is a national not-for-profit organization that provides accessible reading services to the approximately 5 million people across Canada with print disabilities. CELA provides access to a collection of over 1.5 million titles in multiple accessible formats, including audio, braille, printbraille and text.
Short Description: Provides access to a collection of over 1.5 million titles in multiple accessible formats, including audio, braille, printbraille and text.
Eligibility Criteria: People with print disabilities living in Canada. A print disability is a disability that prevents or inhibits a person from reading a literary, musical, dramatic, or artistic work in its original format. Examples of print disability can be: learning disability (e.g., an impairment relating to comprehension), physical disability (the inability to hold or manipulate a book), or visual disability (severe or total impairment of sight)
How to Access: Register online for your local public library's CELA service, or ask for help at your public library. You can register online here: https://celalibrary.ca/register. You can also call or email CELA for support.

They do not put limits on sessions and we make specialized services like EMDR and assessment available too.

Program/Service Description: In-home care services include: daily care support (assistance with hygiene, grooming, and daily routines), household support (light housekeeping, meal prep), senior care (companionship and support), dementia and Alzheimer's care, and specialized medical care.
Short Description: In-home care services include: daily care support, household support, senior care, and more.
How to Access: Contact organizers to book a free consultation. You can fill out the contact form here: https://curavitahomecare.ca/contact/
Cost Details: Eligible client receive services at zero cost through Care Delivery and Home Care Integration (CDHCI). Costs may vary by service.

Program/Service Description: Curio offers counselling for individuals, couples, and families both online and in person. Sliding scale options are available.
Short Description: Curio offers counselling for individuals, couples, and families both online and in person.
How to Access: Book a free, 20 minute consultation online, or contact organizers: https://curiocounselling.janeapp.com/
Cost Details: Fees are offered on a sliding scale basis

Program/Service Description: Come join us for a friendly game or cribbage, whist or your favourite card game. Join for a friendly afternoon of Cards every second Wednesday in the Boardroom or Alpine Room. Various games are played depending upon interest.
Short Description: Cribbage, whist, and other card games are held every second Wednesday.

Program/Service Description: The Danish Canadian Club of Calgary hosts regular events throughout the year, including: Hygge, dinner and dance, holiday events, and more
Short Description: Events include: Hygge, dinner and dance, holiday events, and more

Program/Service Description: Deaf & Hear Alberta offers regular American Sign Language (ASL) courses online and in-person. ASL courses are a “no voice zone”,  full immersion classes taught by qualified Deaf instructors, whose first language is American Sign Language. Financial assistance for adults who cannot afford these programs is available
Short Description: American Sign Language (ASL) courses are offered online and in-person.
Cost Details: Cost varies by program. Financial assistance is available (contact organizers)
Address: 63 Cornell Road NW, Calgary, AB T2L 0L4

Program/Service Description: Getting counselling and other mental health help can be hard for Deaf people. DHA can assist you in finding a mental health expert who communicates in a way that suits you best. Contact to learn more
Short Description: Assistance in finding a mental health expert that are suited for Deaf people.
Address: 63 Cornell Road NW, Calgary, AB T2L 0L4

Program/Service Description: Accessibility Consultants can connect with you to answer questions about home, communication, hearing, and safety devices. They can guide you through the process of finding funding and applying for support. Conversations are fully accessible with ASL interpreters available and live captions.
Short Description: Answer questions about home, communication, hearing, and safety devices for Deaf individuals.
How to Access: Call or text to book an appointment in office, on Zoom, via Video Relay Service, or by phone
Cost Details: Consultations are free. Cost of equipment varies
Address: 63 Cornell Road NW, Calgary, AB T2L 0L4

Program/Service Description: This program brings together socially isolated older adults (55+) who are Deaf or hard of hearing in Alberta. It offers activities like group mentoring, workshops with experts, social gatherings, and one-on-one help with technology. These activities are based on what people want and need.
Short Description: Social program for older adults (55+) who are Deaf or hard of hearing through workshops, social gatherings, technology help, and more.
Eligibility Criteria: Older adult (55+) Deaf or hard of hearing
Address: 63 Cornell Road NW, Calgary, AB T2L 0L4

Program/Service Description: Deaf & Hear Alberta can refer you to Disability Tax Results (DTR) for a free, no-obligation consultation to help you understand whether you may qualify for the Disability Tax Credit (DTC). DTR Specializes in cases that were previously denied; Helps with appeals and re-applications; Charges no upfront fees (success-based only); Explains everything in clear, simple terms
Short Description: Free, no-obligation consultation to help you understand whether you may qualify for the Disability Tax Credit (DTC).
Eligibility Criteria: You may qualify for the tax credit if: Hearing aids do not fully resolve communication barriers; Hearing loss affects work, communication, or daily activities; Hearing loss exists alongside mental health or other conditions
Address: 63 Cornell Road NW, Calgary, AB T2L 0L4

Program/Service Description: Dementia Network Calgary hosts regular events for people with dementia and caregivers. Check their events page for regular updates
Short Description: Regular events for people with dementia and caregivers.
Eligibility Criteria: People living with dementia, family, and caregivers
Address: 7015 Macleod Trail SW #800, Calgary, AB, T2H 2K6

Short Description: Informal, drop-in gathering for people with dementia and their care partners to enjoy conversation and find mutual support.
Eligibility Criteria: People living with dementia, family, and caregivers

Program/Service Description: Dementia Network Calgary promote initiatives, research, advocacy, and learning opportunities that aim to improve the lives of people impacted by dementia in Calgary and area. You can take action by sharing, participating in, or volunteering for any of the projects listed here.
Short Description: Promotes initiatives, research, advocacy, and learning opportunities that aim to improve the lives of people impacted by dementia.
Cost Details: Honorarium may be provided for participating in research

Email: Contact project teams directly listed on website

Short Description: Brings together community insights, research, and real-world resources to support dementia-informed practice.

Program/Service Description: This is a downsizing and relocation service exclusively for older adults. Services include: Moving services (space planning, packing, moving, unpacking, tv and picture hanging), estate sales, gifting and donation, removal and disposal of items, organization assistance, and more.
Short Description: Downsizing and relocation service exclusively for older adults.
How to Access: Get free quote online or contact organizers

Program/Service Description: Distress Centre provides 24 hour crisis support by phone, text and chat to Calgary and southern Alberta. Anyone can contact Distress Centre when they’re in crisis to speak with a highly trained responder, receive emotional support and feel heard. All conversations are confidential.
Short Description: 24 hour crisis support by phone, text and chat to Calgary and southern Alberta.
How to Access: Phone, text, or online chat. To begin online chat, select the message icon in the bottom right of the screen.

Program/Service Description: 9-8-8 is a national three-digit helpline that provides urgent, live support by phone and text for anyone who is thinking about suicide, seeking crisis support, or who is worried about someone they know. Distress Centre Calgary is a 9-8-8 partner and part of the network of crisis lines across the country whose responders take 9-8-8 calls and texts.
Short Description: National helpline that provides support by phone and text for anyone who is thinking about suicide or who is worried about someone they know.

Program/Service Description: Community Bridge Programs promote opportunities and settlement support for visible minorities and new immigrant older adults to promote social inclusion. Programs and activities include: Lion Dance Club, Newcomer's Group, Buddy Program, Women's Group, Mandarin Group, and Supportive Counselling Service
Short Description: Promote opportunities and settlement support for visible minorities and new immigrant older adults such as: dance club, buddy program, women's group, and more.
Eligibility Criteria: Visible minority and/or newcomer older adults (50+)
How to Access: You can register for some programs online, other programs require contact to organizers

Program/Service Description: The Law and Advocacy Program is dedicated to helping individuals, especially immigrants and newcomers, better understand their rights and access the legal system with confidence. Diversecties offer culturally responsive services designed to address language, cultural, and systemic barriers. Services include: Legal information inquiries, one-on-one support, referral services, legal education presentations, and community events.
Short Description: Supporting individuals, especially immigrants and newcomers, navigate the legal system.
Eligibility Criteria: Visibile minorities, marginalized groups, immigrants and newcomers

Program/Service Description: DownsizeFirst is an older adult-specific service to support with transitioning into different living situations. Services include: Planning, downsizing/organizing, dispersal of items, packing and moving, setting up in new home, decluttering, and clearout
Short Description: Older adult-specific service to support with moving and downsizing.
Cost Details: Consultations are free. Cost of services varies

Program/Service Description: Provides individual or charter transportation for individuals with disabilities in Calgary and the surrounding areas.  Services include transportation to medical appointments, charters (across Alberta), and special events. Uses commercial busses and wheelchair accessible busses for transport.
Short Description: Provides individual or charter transportation for individuals with disabilities in Calgary and the surrounding areas.
How to Access: Complete contact form: https://www.dreamstransportation.ca/bookings. Or call organizers
Cost Details: Depends on distance travelled. Weekly and monthly rates negotiable. Group rates available

Program/Service Description: Provides non-medical older adult services offering assistance, accompaniment, and incidental transportation for older adults and those with disabilities or special needs. Will provide transportation services for appointments, errands, and social events.
Short Description: Provides non-medical older adult services offering assistance, accompaniment, and transportation for older adults and those with disabilities.
How to Access: Call individual drivers located in your area by searching on this map: https://drivingmissdaisy.ca/find-location/. Alternatively, call 1-877-613-2479 for more information
Cost Details: Call to get a quote, price calculated by Km
Phone: SW Calgary (403)-888-6391 (Irene), Downtown & NE (403)-464-1432 (Shaugn). Head office phone: 1-877-613-2479

Program/Service Description: Dying with Dignity Canada, Calgary Chapter, meets regularly to provide in-person and virtual events, presentations, and workshops on end-of-life choices. They also host local resources for advance care planning
Short Description: In-person and virtual events, presentations, and workshops on end-of-life choices.

Program/Service Description: ElderDog provides a range of assistance and support, including: Assisting seniors with exercising their dogs; Delivering or picking up dog food from a grocery or pet store; Providing light tasks associated with animal hygiene; Grooming such as nail clipping or help with brushing; Transportation to and from vet or groomer; Temporary care during hospitalization. ElderDog volunteers visit seniors at home and help with basic dog care activities.
Short Description: Services include: Assistance with exercising dogs, food pickup and delivery, nail clipping, transportation to groomers, and more.

Program/Service Description: For older dogs who have lost a human companion due to a residence change, or who are left without a caregiver due to illness or death, ElderDog works to provide care and companionship through: Foster care in an approved foster home; Adoption to an approved home.
Short Description: Connects older dogs who have lost their human companion through foster care and adoption.
Eligibility Criteria: For dogs to be eligible for long-term care in the ElderDog Dog Care Program, they may: Be 10 years or older – age criteria may vary depending on breed/size (long-term and perpetual care planning is available for younger dogs); Have worked in a service/caregiving capacity; Have no history of aggression; Have experienced or are about to experience a disruption in their lives due to change in residence, human companion illness or death; Live with an elderly human companion who needs dog care assistance in order to stay together; Have care needs that can no longer be adequately provided; Face health and/or mobility challenges; Be deemed “unadoptable” by an animal shelter or humane society due to age, mobility, or state of health
How to Access: Contact organizers. If you want to foster or adopt an older dog, complete application online and a re-homing coordinator will set up a telephone conversation

Program/Service Description: If you become unable to care for your dog, ElderDog Canada commits to place your dog in a loving forever home to live out her/his life with respect and dignity.
Short Description: Rehoming dogs for owners who are unable to care for their pet.
Eligibility Criteria: Older adult no longer able to care for your dog
How to Access: Contact organizers or complete form online

Organization: Elizz Caregiver Support and Home Care Services
Program/Service Description: Provides in-home care and virtual services.Types of services offered: Personal care (daily activities, mobility, exercise, feeding, medication management, companionship), help at home (meal planning and preparation, grocery shopping, laundry, light housekeeping, accompanying to appointments), nursing care, dementia care, respite care
Short Description: In-home care services include: daily activities, mobility, exercise, feeding, housekeeping, transportation, and more.

Organization: Elizz Caregiver Support and Home Care Services
Program/Service Description: Whether you are new to the role of caregiver or if your loved one’s needs have changed, an Elizz Care Navigator can help guide and support you. They can support with resource navigation, balancing your schedule, managing difficult conversations, and provide information about dementia and end of life care.
Short Description: Support with caregiver resource navigation, balancing schedules, having difficult conversations, and more.
How to Access: Request a session online or contact organizers. A one-time, one hour session is free.
Cost Details: Cost unknown. One-time sessions are free, or you can sign up for a monthly subscription

Program/Service Description: The Evergreen Seniors Outdoor Club provides seniors (55 years and over) in the Calgary area with opportunities to walk, hike, snowshoe or cross-country ski in the mountains year round. Travel by bus most Thursdays at 8am to the mountains or foothills. You can join as a member or a guest. New events are posted regularly on their website
Short Description: Opportunities to walk, hike, snowshoe or cross-country ski in the mountains year round.
How to Access: Once you have come out three times as a guest on the bus, you are eligible to apply for membership.
Cost Details: Bus fare: $25.00. For trips into a national park, there is an additional $10 charge if one doesn't have an annual pass. Cost of membership is unknown
Address: Bus departs from the Montgomery Community Association parking lot on Home Road and 16th Avenue NW. 5003 16 Ave NW

Program/Service Description: Provides in clinic and mobile foot care. Services include: foot assessment, diabetic foot care, callus and corn reduction, ingrown and fungal toenail treatment, basic wound care, foot health education.
Short Description: Provides in clinic and mobile foot care. Services include: foot assessment, diabetic foot care, callus and corn reduction, and more.
How to Access: Contact organizers by phone, email, or website to book appointment
Address: 11 Royal Vista Dr NW #3140, Calgary, AB T3R 0N2

Program/Service Name: Connect Domestic Violence and Abuse Helpline
Program/Service Description: The Connect Domestic Violence and Abuse Helpline is often the first contact for people reaching out for support. Helpline counsellors answer the phone 24 hours per day, 365 days a year. They provide counselling, safety planning, referrals and information in multiple languages.
Short Description: 24/7 help line for people reaching out for support related to domestic abuse. Information is provided in multiple languages.
Eligibility Criteria: Individuals who have or are currently experiencing domestic violence and abuse

Program/Service Description: Call the Men's Resource Line to explore concerns related to domestic violence and develop and implement solutions that change behaviour. Phones are open 24/7 and handled by trained counsellors who can answer questions and support with accessing the right services for you.
Short Description: 24/7 help line for men about concerns related to domestic violence.

Program/Service Description: The Court Program provides navigation of the Family Law system and support for individuals who have or are currently experiencing domestic violence and abuse.  Participation in the program increases preparedness to interact with the Family court system and connections to the appropriate professionals to assist people to navigate the court system. The Court Case Coordinator: Provides information and guidance to navigate the court process (Family Law); Assists with safety planning; Offers referrals for identified needs, including legal advocacy; Accompanies clients to court and connects them with necessary court personnel; Helps to navigate court paperwork.
Short Description: Provides navigation of the Family Law system and support for individuals who have or are currently experiencing domestic violence and abuse.
Eligibility Criteria: Individuals who have or are currently experiencing domestic violence and abuse

Program/Service Description: FearIsNotLove offers voluntary individual therapy sessions and group counselling services to adults interested in creating or enhancing safety in their close relationships. They support people in addressing their hurtful controlling or abusive behaviours and the problems this has caused. Counsellors contact the partners or ex-partners of the people who are attending counselling, in order to understand their concerns about the person’s behaviour, any progress they are noticing, and to monitor safety. You can access up to twelve sessions or six months of counselling, whichever point is reached first.
Short Description: Voluntary individual therapy sessions and group counselling services to adults to address their controlling or abusive behaviours.
Eligibility Criteria: This program is not just for men. Any adult who want support to address their controlling or abusive behaviours and/or the problems their expression of anger has caused in their relationships are also welcome to contact Men’s Counselling Service.

Program/Service Description: Empowering the Filipino-Canadian community, Filipinos Rising is dedicated to building a resilient and inclusive society. They aim to amplify the voice of community members and influence in shaping a fair and equitable Canada through advocacy, civic engagement, and leadership development. Contact organizers to learn more about programs and services offered.
Short Description: Advocacy, civic engagement, and leadership development to empower the Filipino-Canadian community.
Eligibility Criteria: Programs and services are designed for Filipinx individuals

Program/Service Description: Finding Balance is an education program and public awareness campaign designed to educate and empower older Albertans to stay independent and prevent falls. They offer several free online resources, including: falls risk self-assessment quiz, how to prevent falls, resources for caregivers, activity tips and programming, tips for vision, and a First Nation Elder fall prevention resource.
Short Description: Free online resources for fall prevention, including: falls risk-assessment, caregiver resources, First Nation Elder fall prevention resource, and more.

Short Description: Activities include: acting, bridge, art sessions, bus tours, calligraphy, photography, casino, coffee group, cribbage, cycling, and more.

Short Description: Events to promote the long term sustainability of Calgary’s historic Chinatown, such as Qi Gong, tshirt making, cooking class, and more.

Short Description: Regular programs include: bridge, floor curling, line dancing, square dancing, bingo, Cards & Coffee, walking, ukulele, yoga, and more.

Program/Service Description: The Office of the Alberta Health Advocates provides support and advocates for a health care system that is responsive and accountable to the people being served. The Office includes a Health Advocate, Mental Health Patient Advocate, and an Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate. Advocates refer people to the appropriate programs and services to address their complaints. They have the ability to conduct investigations or reviews into specific complaints related to mental health patient rights and the Alberta Health Charter. The Advocates help educate Albertans about the mental health patient rights set out in the Mental Health Act and the expectations of the Alberta Health Charter.
Short Description: Provides support and advocates for individuals navigating the healthcare system.
How to Access: Call the Advocate Office, or submit an online inquiry here: https://www.alberta.ca/contact-the-health-advocates.aspx
Address:
106th Street Tower – 9th Floor
10055 106 Street
Edmonton AB  T5J 2Y2
Determinant: ["Stay Safe", "Stay Healthy", "Get Help", "Manage Money & Legal Matters"]

Clients pay a basic rate and youth within the community shovel snow and receive their pay through the Haysboro Community Association. Program/Service Description: JFSC provides social welfare services for eligible Holocaust survivors through funding from The Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany (Claims Conference). They address emergency financial and home support needs and look for solutions to support individuals to live independently as long as possible by providing: Support to eligible Holocaust Survivors with assistance to apply for any compensation or pensions from the Claims Conference and/or German government; Home Support Services; Connection to cultural and social supports; Support in applying for additional resources offered by government agencies; Advocacy.
Short Description: Provides social welfare services for eligible Holocaust survivors including: Compensation, home support services, government application support, and more.
Eligibility Criteria: A Holocaust survivor is considered a person who suffered persecution for being Jewish, lived in a Ghetto, survived a concentration camp and/or who had to flee or evacuate from the place of persecution.

Program/Service Description: JFSC provides short and/or long-term support and can assist with physical and/or emotional limitations that impact daily living. Short Description: Provides short and/or long-term support and can assist with physical and/or emotional limitations that impact daily living.

Program/Service Description: The Tech Safe program is designed to support technologically inexperienced older adults with group and one-on-one support with their devices, to better understand technology, their personal devices and how to avoid being subject to scams or financial exploitation. Short Description: Supports technologically inexperienced older adults with group and one-on-one support with their devices, to better understand technology, and how to avoid scams.

Short Description: One-on-one with clients to address the effects of poverty, including: needs assessment, food pantry, financial coaching, and more.

Program/Service Description: The “Seniors in the Loop” Group gets together in the Marda Loop Community Association Upper Hall on the first Monday of each month except when it falls on a statutory holiday. They take a break for Summer, but still meet for walks, picnics, plays, movies or pool parties etc. either in small or large groups. These get-togethers start at 9 am with 45 minute of light exercise. This is followed by presentations by experts from various fields of interest to seniors with an opportunity to meet one-on-one with these knowledgeable individuals. An hour or so of social interaction and board games, singing, ping pong etc. follows till 12:30 pm. Snacks and refreshments are provided by volunteers.
Short Description: Monthly group that meet up for walks, picnics, plays, movies, pool parties, etc, followed by presentations by experts from various fields.

Program/Service Description: Heritage Time Out is an opportunity for women to get together to socialize, have a coffee and take time for themselves to enjoy doing a craft. Participants bring their own supplies; there is a choice of activities: embroidery, knitting, crochet, quilting, cardmaking, as well as a “do as you wish” which can be any project you have on the go. They meet Wednesday mornings, 9-11:30 am during the school year in the Hospitality Hall.
Short Description: Opportunity for women to get together to socialize, have a coffee and take time for themselves to enjoy doing a craft.

Program/Service Description: Opera Buddies is an intergenerational opera discovery program for youth, adults, and older adults. You’ll connect with other lifelong learners of all ages interested in broadening their musical horizons or deepening their love of opera. Each Opera Buddies session begins with two classes: an introduction to opera as well as a primer on the opera you’ll be going to see. You’ll learn what to expect at the theatre, as well as insights into what to watch and listen for at the show. Then, come to the opera and watch the performance with a live orchestra, soloists, and chorus.
Short Description: Intergenerational opera discovery program for youth, adults, and older adults.

Program/Service Description: Throughout a six-week session, attendees convene on a weekly basis to acquire fundamental mental health concepts, engage in discussions, and partake in mutual learning. They also develop coping skills to manage everyday stresses effectively. Facilitating this program is an experienced Clinical Counsellor, and it is available in three languages: English, Mandarin, and Cantonese.​ It is held on Zoom and includes a free comprehensive self-care kit, a 1-hour individual session with the counsellor, an an in-person group review session after course completion.
Short Description: 6-week sessions to learn about mental health concepts, develop stress coping skills, and engage in discussions. Offered in English, Mandarin and Cantonese.
How to Access: Contact organizers or register online at bottom of the page

Program/Service Description: This program is designed to empower seniors with the vital language skills needed to thrive independently within the community, focusing on Practical English language proficiency. Topics are organized around critical areas of independent living and in each class, seniors learn practical terminology, vocabulary, usage and application of the language they have learned. Each series of learning is organized at the Beginner and Intermediate levels. Key topics covered include: English for banking and finance, English for digital communication, English for independent living, and English for women's health
Short Description: Practical English language classes for older adults, organized around important and practical topic areas.

Program/Service Description: PLAN Calgary is a non-profit parent-led organization,whose main objective is to secure the future of people of all abilities by creating a good life now and in the future. A Personal Support Network is a group of people who meet together to become the foundation of a family’s Future Plan. They carry out roles and responsibilities that are difficult for the friend or relative with a disability to carry out on their own. For some, this will mean practical assistance with housing, employment and recreation. For others it will mean developing closer ties to neighbors and the community. The Personal Support Network Development Process involves PLAN Calgary’s trained Community Connectors getting to know the family and their loved one, and working with them to develop the Personal Support Network. While the Community Connector is paid, the people involved in a Personal Support Network are not. Their involvement is based on caring and loving friendships, and a commitment to work together on behalf of the person with a disability. Networks can include siblings, other family, friends, neighbors, church members, co-workers and occasionally a professional service provider.
Short Description: Personal support networks meet together to help an individual with a disability develop a future plan.
Eligibility Criteria: People with disabilities (type of disability unspecified) and caregivers

Although the group is intended mainly for those living alone, the primary purpose is connection. Couples whose social opportunities have perhaps become limited due to health or mobility challenges are also very welcome.

Often there are speakers or videos which are of general interest to seniors.  The socials are advertised in the Church Bulletin.  New members are always welcome
Short Description: Social group for adults over 50 in the Parish. The group enjoys card games and other social events.

Program/Service Description: St. Stephen’s choir ministry is actively involved in the Sunday liturgies and encourages all members of the congregation to join in singing.  In addition to Sunday liturgies, the choir (well over 60 members) is present to respond to services including the celebration of weddings, the farewell of loved ones during funerals and many events throughout the course of the church year. There is no requirement of singing or musical experience and there is no expectation to learn notes or the Ukrainian language. The choir typically rehearses on Wednesday evenings; in addition they gather each year over the Christmas season to carol with other choirs as part of an annual televised Ukrainian carol festival.
Short Description: Choir ministry is actively involved in the Sunday liturgies. They typically rehearse on Wednesday evenings.

Program/Service Name: Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada (LINC)
Program/Service Description:
YMCA Calgary offers English language classes for newcomers to Canada that focuses on improving communication by developing, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. There are a variety of part-time classes during the day and in the evenings. Classes focus on themes relevant to newcomers such as Canadian culture, banking, community services, education, family, and getting around the city. Participants also take field trips, learn computer skills, volunteer, and participate in health and wellness activities as offered by YMCA Calgary. 

Classes are held at the Saddletown, Shane Homes at Rocky Ridge, Shawnessy and South Health Campus YMCA locations.
Short Description: English language classes for newcomers to Canada. Participants take field trips, learn computer skills, volunteer and more.
Eligibility Criteria: Those 18 years of age and over with permanent residency, convention refugee status, or protected person status are eligible for the LINC program.
How to Access: Prior to starting LINC classes, students must complete a language assessment through Immigrant Services Calgary. Get started by filling out this form: https://www.immigrantservicescalgary.ca/clarcregistration/

Program/Service Name: Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada
Program/Service Description: Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada (LINC) provides basic English language training to help permanent residents or refugees with social, cultural and economic adaptation. This program is designed to help women and men adjust and build confidence. Participants learn about the local community and Canadian society; develop practical English-language skills, and widen their social circle. LINC classes are organized by Canadian Language Benchmark levels — YW currently offers CLB 1 to CLB 4. LINC classes at YW are part-time and offered as online, in-person or blended learning opportunities.
Short Description: Basic English language training to help permanent residents or refugees with social, cultural and economic adaptation. Part-time and offered online, in-person, or hybrid.
Eligibility Criteria: Adult women and men who are permanent residents, immigrants and refugees to Canada.
